name: Ukraine
note: Ukraine, in the style of the Russian model tree: economy, energy, military, war, foreign policy and society branches build, fix Ukraine's sourced starting spirits (data/spirits/ukr.json), unlock decisions (data/decisions/ukr.json), claim the occupied regions and grant research. The political branch has the historical path (between East and West, then the reforms after 2014) and six mutually exclusive alternatives: an eastern course (the Party of Regions), liberal, left, national, ultranationalist (needs a party of the fascist group, which Ukraine does not have in the data) and a military junta. Each alternative brings to power only a real party of the data. Alternatives are a counterfactual, not a claim about the parties. Policies named after real reforms are cited; effects are gameplay estimates. Wars stay in data/events/conflicts.json; no focus declares one.

focuses.name: An independent state
focuses.description: Consolidate the institutions of an independent Ukraine.

focuses.name: Between East and West
focuses.description: Balance relations with Russia and the West while the institutions of the new state settle. This is the path Ukraine took.

focuses.name: A parliamentary-presidential republic
focuses.description: Constitutional amendments of 2004 move powers from the President to the Verkhovna Rada and the government. They took force on 1 January 2006.

focuses.name: Presidential powers restored
focuses.description: The Constitutional Court overturns the 2004 amendments in 2010, restoring the earlier presidential powers.

focuses.name: Civil society
focuses.description: Independent media, election monitors and civic groups grow after the protests of 2004.

focuses.name: After the Revolution of Dignity
focuses.description: A new government forms after the protests that began on the Maidan on 21 November 2013 and the President's removal in February 2014.

focuses.name: Decentralisation
focuses.description: Give amalgamated communities (hromadas) their own budgets and powers, a reform launched on 1 April 2014.

focuses.name: A new national police
focuses.description: Replace the militsiya with the National Police, formed on 3 July 2015.

focuses.name: National Anti-Corruption Bureau
focuses.description: An independent bureau that investigates corruption among officials; its first detectives started work on 1 October 2015.

focuses.name: ProZorro public procurement
focuses.description: An open electronic system for public procurement, developed with civil society and business.

focuses.name: The Euro-Atlantic course in the constitution
focuses.description: The Verkhovna Rada amends the constitution on 7 February 2019 to name membership of the EU and NATO as strategic goals.

focuses.name: Wartime unity
focuses.description: Parties and regions rally behind the government in a war for the country's survival.

focuses.name: Eastern course
focuses.description: Seek a close partnership with Russia; the Party of Regions, strongest in the east and south, leads the way.

focuses.name: Rally the east and south
focuses.description: Organise industrial workers and Russian-speaking voters behind the Party of Regions.

focuses.name: A Party of Regions government
focuses.description: The Party of Regions forms the government.

focuses.name: Status for the Russian language
focuses.description: Give Russian official status in the regions where most people speak it.

focuses.name: Eurasian integration
focuses.description: Join the economic projects led by Russia instead of the European Union.

focuses.name: Liberal breakthrough
focuses.description: New liberal parties win over voters tired of the old elites.

focuses.name: Clean politics
focuses.description: Campaign against the influence of business owners on parliament.

focuses.name: A liberal government
focuses.description: The most popular liberal party forms the government.

focuses.name: Deregulation
focuses.description: Cut licences and inspections for small businesses.

focuses.name: Open government
focuses.description: Publish budgets, contracts and officials' declarations online.

focuses.name: Red revival
focuses.description: Falling wages and pensions turn voters toward the Communist Party of Ukraine and the other parties of the left.

focuses.name: Pensioners and workers
focuses.description: Rallies of pensioners and factory workers behind the left.

focuses.name: A government of the left
focuses.description: The most popular socialist party takes power and rules as the single governing party.

focuses.name: Renationalisation
focuses.description: Return the privatised steel works and mines to public ownership.

focuses.name: Fraternal ties
focuses.description: Close ties with Russia and Belarus.

focuses.name: National awakening
focuses.description: National-democratic and nationalist parties such as Rukh gain ground on questions of language, history and Russia.

focuses.name: Language and memory
focuses.description: Promote Ukrainian in public life and a national reading of history.

focuses.name: A national government
focuses.description: The most popular nationalist party forms the government.

focuses.name: Energy sovereignty
focuses.description: End dependence on Russian gas whatever the cost.

focuses.name: An armed nation
focuses.description: Universal military training and a large reserve.

focuses.name: Ultranationalist turn
focuses.description: In a deep crisis, an ultranationalist party gains a mass following and seeks an authoritarian state. This is a counterfactual, not a claim about the party's aims. Available only where such a party exists in the data.

focuses.name: A street movement
focuses.description: Marches and rallies spread the movement in the cities.

focuses.name: Seizure of power
focuses.description: The ultranationalist party takes power, abolishes elections and rules as the only party.

focuses.name: Total mobilisation
focuses.description: State control of the press and the economy for war.

focuses.name: The army steps in
focuses.description: With the state in crisis, the generals prepare to take over.

focuses.name: Military council
focuses.description: The armed forces remove the government. The coup may fail.

focuses.name: Martial order
focuses.description: A state of emergency, a curfew and military courts.

focuses.name: Return to the barracks
focuses.description: The council hands power to an elected government.

focuses.name: Economic recovery
focuses.description: Return to growth after a decade of decline.

focuses.name: Stabilise the hryvnia
focuses.description: Tight money and an independent central bank end the inflation of the 1990s.

focuses.name: Large-scale privatisation
focuses.description: Sell the large state enterprises to private owners.

focuses.name: Tax reform
focuses.description: Simplify taxes and widen the base.

focuses.name: Clean up the banks
focuses.description: Close insolvent banks and strengthen the central bank's supervision.

focuses.name: An IMF programme
focuses.description: Loans from the International Monetary Fund in exchange for reforms.

focuses.name: Steel and coal
focuses.description: Modernise the steel works and mines of the east.

focuses.name: A full recovery
focuses.description: The recovery is secure and the banks are sound.

focuses.name: Free trade with the EU
focuses.description: The trade part of the Association Agreement, a deep and comprehensive free trade area, applies from 1 January 2016.

focuses.name: Grain and oilseed exports
focuses.description: Invest in grain and sunflower-oil exports through the Black Sea ports.

focuses.name: A farmland market
focuses.description: Allow the sale of farmland.

focuses.name: Information technology
focuses.description: Tax incentives for software and IT services.

focuses.name: Food processing
focuses.description: Process grain and oilseeds at home.

focuses.name: Reconstruction
focuses.description: Rebuild housing, power and transport damaged by war.

focuses.name: Energy strategy
focuses.description: Plan the country's energy for the coming decades.

focuses.name: Domestic gas
focuses.description: Raise gas output from the fields of Poltava and Kharkiv.

focuses.name: Energy efficiency
focuses.description: Insulate homes and meter heat and gas to cut consumption.

focuses.name: Ports and railways
focuses.description: Modernise the Black Sea ports and the railways to the west.

focuses.name: Reverse gas flows
focuses.description: Import gas from the west through the pipelines that once carried it only one way.

focuses.name: Nuclear fuel diversification
focuses.description: Buy fuel for the nuclear power plants from more than one supplier.

focuses.name: Roads to Europe
focuses.description: Motorways and border crossings to Poland and Romania.

focuses.name: Aerospace industry
focuses.description: Aircraft and engines from the plants of Kyiv, Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia.

focuses.name: Wind and solar
focuses.description: Wind and solar farms in the south.

focuses.name: Machine building
focuses.description: Tractors, turbines and rail cars for export.

focuses.name: Join the European grid
focuses.description: Synchronise the power grid with continental Europe.

focuses.name: Industrial parks
focuses.description: Serviced land and tax breaks for new plants in the west.

focuses.name: Defence review
focuses.description: Review the armed forces inherited from the Soviet Union.

focuses.name: A smaller, better army
focuses.description: Cut the size of the forces and spend more per soldier.

focuses.name: Contract soldiers
focuses.description: More professional soldiers alongside conscripts.

focuses.name: Border guard
focuses.description: Strengthen the border guard on the eastern and southern borders.

focuses.name: NATO standards
focuses.description: Train and organise the forces to NATO standards.

focuses.name: Defence industry
focuses.description: Restart production of armoured vehicles, missiles and ammunition at home. Unlocks defence orders.

focuses.name: Rebuild the navy
focuses.description: A navy and coastal defences based in Odesa and Mykolaiv instead of Sevastopol.

focuses.name: Armoured vehicles
focuses.description: Modernise tanks and armoured vehicles at the Kharkiv and Kyiv plants.

focuses.name: Missiles and artillery
focuses.description: Domestic missiles and artillery ammunition.

focuses.name: Air defence
focuses.description: Modernise and extend air defence around cities and power plants.

focuses.name: Drones
focuses.description: Reconnaissance and strike drones built by domestic firms and volunteers.

focuses.name: Special operations forces
focuses.description: A separate command for special operations.

focuses.name: A trained reserve
focuses.description: Regular refresher training for former soldiers.

focuses.name: The defence of Ukraine
focuses.description: Organise the country's defence after the annexation of Crimea and the start of the war in the Donbas in 2014.

focuses.name: Volunteer battalions into the army
focuses.description: Bring the volunteer battalions under the command of the armed forces and the National Guard.

focuses.name: Fortify the Donbas front
focuses.description: Trenches and strongpoints along the line of contact.

focuses.name: Crimea is Ukraine
focuses.description: Ukraine does not recognise the annexation of Crimea and claims it back.

focuses.name: Territorial Defence Forces
focuses.description: Volunteer reservists organised in every region, a separate branch of the armed forces from January 2022.

focuses.name: Western military aid
focuses.description: Training, intelligence and weapons from NATO members.

focuses.name: The occupied regions
focuses.description: Claim back every region Russia or its proxies hold.

focuses.name: A wartime economy
focuses.description: Put the economy on a war footing.

focuses.name: Long-range strikes
focuses.description: Drones and missiles that reach depots and airfields far behind the front.

focuses.name: Deny the Black Sea
focuses.description: Coastal missiles and sea drones push the Russian fleet away from the coast.

focuses.name: Energy resilience
focuses.description: Repair and protect the power grid under attack.

focuses.name: Prepare a counteroffensive
focuses.description: Train and equip new brigades for an offensive.

focuses.name: Foreign policy priorities
focuses.description: Set the course of foreign policy for an independent Ukraine.

focuses.name: European choice
focuses.description: Make membership of the European Union the long-term goal.

focuses.name: Eurasian choice
focuses.description: Tie the economy to Russia and its partners instead.

focuses.name: Kharkiv agreements
focuses.description: Extend the lease of the Russian Black Sea Fleet's base in Crimea to 2042 in exchange for discounted gas, as agreed on 21 April 2010.

focuses.name: A NATO perspective
focuses.description: Seek a path to NATO membership; at the Bucharest summit in April 2008 the allies agreed that Ukraine would become a member, without a Membership Action Plan.

focuses.name: Association Agreement with the EU
focuses.description: Sign the Association Agreement with the European Union: political provisions on 21 March 2014, provisional application from 1 November 2014, full force on 1 September 2017.

focuses.name: A customs union in the east
focuses.description: Join a customs union with Russia and its partners.

focuses.name: Minsk agreements
focuses.description: Ceasefire agreements for the Donbas signed in September 2014 and on 12 February 2015.

focuses.name: Partnership with Poland
focuses.description: A close partnership with Poland as the gateway to the European Union.

focuses.name: EU candidate status
focuses.description: The European Council grants Ukraine candidate status on 23 June 2022.

focuses.name: A long-term gas deal with Russia
focuses.description: Cheap gas for a long-term transit contract.

focuses.name: A sanctions coalition
focuses.description: Rally partners to keep economic pressure on Russia.

focuses.name: Black Sea grain exports
focuses.description: Keep the sea route for grain exports open.

focuses.name: Social policy
focuses.description: Set the government's priorities for health, schools and science.

focuses.name: Health reform
focuses.description: Money follows the patient; family doctors and new hospitals.

focuses.name: The new Ukrainian school
focuses.description: A twelve-year school with new curricula.

focuses.name: A state in a smartphone
focuses.description: Public services online, from documents to permits.

focuses.name: Research institutes
focuses.description: Fund the academy's institutes and the universities.

focuses.name: Care for veterans
focuses.description: Rehabilitation, housing and jobs for veterans.

focuses.name: Help for the displaced
focuses.description: Housing and work for people who fled the war zones.
